summary: Go SDK ignores Retry-After on 429 and retries too quickly (rate limit / thundering herd risk)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports Go SDK does not respect Retry-After on 429 responses. Instead it retries immediately (or with minimal delay), causing rapid repeat 429s and increased load.

Impact
- Customer sees prolonged periods of throttling and elevated request volume from their clients during 429 bursts.
- Risk of “retry storm” / thundering herd when many workers hit 429 simultaneously.
- Inconsistent behavior vs TS/Python expectations (customer has mixed-language services).

Customer report (Northwind AI)
- Workload: ~200 goroutines sending chat completions for background enrichment jobs.
- Behavior: when rate limit kicks in, Go clients retry too fast and never recover until they reduce concurrency manually.
- Expectation: SDK should honor Retry-After header and back off.

Environment
- Prod, us-east
- Go SDK version: v0.9.6 (per customer)

Steps to reproduce (internal)
1) Use Go SDK with default retry settings.
2) Send burst traffic until gateway returns 429.
3) Observe retry timing. Expected: delay >= Retry-After (plus jitter). Actual: delay appears ~0–200ms and repeats.

Evidence / logs
- Customer-provided snippet (redacted):
  - 429 responses include header: Retry-After: 8
  - request_id present in body but not surfaced by SDK error

- Internal repro (from Support):
  - curl shows Retry-After header is present on 429 from api.redwoodinference.com:
    - HTTP/2 429
    - retry-after: 10
    - x-request-id: req_01JH9P7K9X2R2D5RZK...
  - Go SDK debug output shows retry loop delay does not incorporate Retry-After.

Notes
- This aligns with ongoing SDK parity initiative for standardized retries/timeouts.
- Need to confirm whether the Go SDK parses both Retry-After formats:
  (a) integer seconds
  (b) HTTP-date

Requested outcome
- Go SDK should:
  - Treat 429 as retryable by default (already does)
  - Respect Retry-After if present (seconds or date)
  - Clamp to a sane max (per standard) and apply jitter around the chosen delay
  - Surface request_id on the raised error for triage

Suggested fix (high level)
- In Go retry middleware, when response status == 429:
  - Parse Retry-After header:
    - If integer seconds: sleep that duration
    - Else attempt HTTP-date parse and compute delta from now
  - Use max(parsed_delay, exponential_backoff_delay) to avoid retrying sooner than policy
  - Apply jitter (full jitter or equal jitter per standard) without going below parsed_delay

Gateway/header verification
- Verify gateway emits Retry-After consistently on 429 for both streaming and non-streaming paths.
- If missing in some cases, coordinate with platform to add it (but initial checks show it exists).

2026-01-29 09:18 (Owen Phillips, Support) — Ticket opened from customer escalation. Customer says Go SDK retries “immediately” on 429 even though they see Retry-After in response headers via a proxy log. Asking for: SDK version, sample request_id(s), and whether they’re using streaming.

2026-01-29 10:25 (Owen Phillips, Support) — Reproduced with a burst script. curl shows gateway returns Retry-After on 429 in prod us-east. Go SDK retries much sooner than the header value. Attaching repro notes to internal Slack thread #support (ref: 1768110400).

2026-01-29 11:10 (Mateusz Zielinski, Go SDK) — Acknowledged. Quick scan: current retry loop uses exponential backoff only and does not consult Retry-After. Will patch to parse both numeric seconds and HTTP-date. Will align with parity retry standard (max attempts, jitter) as part of ongoing work.

2026-01-29 11:28 (Allison Grant, SRE) — +1 to respecting Retry-After. Please ensure jitter does not reduce below Retry-After delay (avoid synchronized retries). Also recommend clamping extreme Retry-After values (e.g., >60s) per standard and surfacing retry_count for logs.

2026-01-30 14:05 (Mateusz Zielinski, Go SDK) — Implemented fix on branch. Behavior: on 429, compute baseDelay = max(expBackoff, retryAfterDelay). Apply equal-jitter around baseDelay but never below baseDelay. Also propagating request_id into error type when present.

2026-02-03 09:42 (Owen Phillips, Support) — Verified gateway Retry-After presence using both:
- /v1/chat/completions (non-streaming)
- /v1/chat/completions?stream=true (streaming)
Observed retry-after present on 429 in both cases. x-request-id present.

2026-02-04 16:20 (Mateusz Zielinski, Go SDK) — PR opened: redwood-sdk-go#612 “retry policy standardization” includes Retry-After parsing + tests. Also includes conformance fixture for 429 + Retry-After=3s.

2026-02-06 13:15 (Owen Phillips, Support) — Sent customer workaround while fix is pending release:
- Reduce concurrency during 429 bursts
- Implement external rate limiting and/or honor Retry-After in application-level retry wrapper
- Temporarily disable SDK retries and handle 429 manually (customer requested this option)

2026-02-10 10:05 (Mateusz Zielinski, Go SDK) — Fix released in Go SDK v0.10.0. Release notes mention: “Respect Retry-After on 429; improved request_id in errors.”

2026-02-10 11:30 (Owen Phillips, Support) — Customer confirmed improved behavior after upgrading to v0.10.0: retry cadence now matches Retry-After and they recover without manual intervention. Closing.

Resolution
- Shipped fix in redwood-sdk-go v0.10.0 (PR: redwood-sdk-go#612)
- Confirmed gateway already emits Retry-After for 429 in prod.

Follow-ups
- Ensure conformance suite includes 429 + Retry-After cases across Python/TS/Go.
- Track request_id propagation consistency (linked: INT-1182).
